payload.title: Prepare go-gitutil for its first tagged release
payload.description: Prepare go-gitutil for its first tagged release: adopt gomion's generated workflows, require published dependency versions with no replace, push to GitHub, and propose a version for the owner to tag.
payload.context: go-gitutil holds git helpers extracted from gomion and has never been tagged. Its go.mod requires go-diffutils at the placeholder v0.0.0 and resolves it, go-dt and go-dt/dtx through replace directives pointing at sibling checkouts, so it builds only on this machine. It has no CI or Release workflow, and tags in go-pkgs are created by a repo's generated Release workflow, never by hand. main has one uncommitted go.mod change raising go-dt. The GitHub repo exists with a single LICENSE-only commit that shares no history with the local commits. Decided: require go-diffutils v0.1.0, its latest tag and identical to its current main; a later go-diffutils tag never forces go-gitutil to re-tag, so there is no reason to wait for one.
payload.analysis: 1. Commit the pending go.mod change. 2. Merge GitHub's LICENSE commit with git merge --allow-unrelated-histories origin/main; never force-push. 3. Require go-diffutils v0.1.0 and the latest tags of go-dt and go-dt/dtx, drop every replace directive, and run go mod tidy. 4. Run gomion repo setup to raise go.mod to Go 1.27 and write test.yml and release.yml; gomion repo setup --check must report the repo up to date. Do not hand-edit the generated files. 5. GOWORK=off go build ./... and GOWORK=off go test ./... pass. 6. Push main; create no tags. 7. Propose a first version (v0.1.0 unless something argues otherwise) and a release description, and report them to the owner, who runs the Release workflow. After the push, the first Test run must show zero Actions warnings and notices.

payload.title: Find directory-prefixed tags in Repo.LatestTag
payload.description: Find directory-prefixed tags in Repo.LatestTag so a nested module's latest tag (such as dtx/v0.2.2) is found and compared by its version part.
payload.context: Repo.Tags filters tags by a module's directory prefix but returns them with the prefix still on. Repo.LatestTag then keeps only tags passing semver.IsValid, which rejects every prefixed tag, so for any nested module LatestTag returns ErrNoSemverTags even when tags exist. gomion has the same code in its own copy of this package and tracks the same bug; its fix is meant to come from here.
payload.analysis: In Repo.LatestTag, strip the module's directory prefix before semver.IsValid and semver comparison, and return the full prefixed tag. Add a test with a nested-module fixture holding prefixed tags, plus a root-module case to show root tags are unaffected.

# Synthesis: what git operations go-gitutil provides for fixtures

Brainstorm with Mike, 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12, with answers relayed from the
gomion (E-2546) and go-fsfix (E-2547/E-2568) sessions. Everything below is
Mike's choice unless marked "proposed" (my proposal he accepted) or "fact".

## The operation set

go-gitutil gains four operations for fixtures and gomion, all on `Repo`:

- `Init(ctx, InitArgs{Branch, Identity})`: `git init -b <branch>`; writes
  `user.name`/`user.email` into the new repo's local config when Identity is set.
- `Clone(ctx, src, CloneArgs{Local, NoCheckout, Branch, Bare, Identity})`:
  exported; cached_worktree.go calls it instead of its private clone. Identity
  is written to the clone's local config, since a clone does not copy the
  source's local config.
- `Add(ctx, AddArgs{Paths, Exclude, All, Force})`: Exclude becomes git pathspec
  magic `:(exclude)<dir>/`, so git filters and no file list is built in Go.
  Force is an ordinary flag, off by default, like git's.
- `Commit(ctx, CommitArgs{Message, Identity, AllowEmpty})`: Identity is passed
  as `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` env for that one process.

Nothing else is new. `RevParse` already reads HEAD. Reset and checkout were
proposed by the E-2568 session for RepoFixture.Reconcile and withdrawn: a
fixture gets clean git state by being recreated (Cleanup then Create), which
measured 41 ms for 10 files and 412 ms for 10,000. Reconcile is disk-only and
never runs git.

## The shape of Repo (Q1, answered via E-2546 and here)

- `NewRepo(dir, RepoArgs) *Repo` constructs with no I/O. Mike: "a NewRepo()
  allows ALWAYS getting a Repo value which can be important for testing or
  other use-cases." He accepts that every other method guards against an
  unopened Repo. His further point: `Repo{}` is always constructible in Go, so
  package-level constructors never protected against an uninitialized value.
- `(*Repo).Open(ctx, OpenArgs) error` does what OpenRepo does today. `Open`,
  not `Initialize`: a type with both `Init` (git init) and `Initialize` (read
  state) is a trap, and people look for Open.
- Package-level `gitutil.Open(ctx, dir, OpenArgs)`, `gitutil.Init(ctx, dir,
  InitArgs)` and `gitutil.Clone(ctx, src, dst, CloneArgs)` each construct a
  Repo and call the method, so the implementation lives once. Both styles are
  offered so callers pick what fits.
- `OpenRepo` is removed, no alias.
- `RepoArgs` holds what describes the Repo for its life: `StdIO dt.StdIO` and
  `Identity`. `OpenArgs` holds what is about the act of opening; empty today,
  kept for evolution.

## Identity (Q2)

- Identity is optional on `RepoArgs`, `InitArgs`, `CloneArgs` and
  `CommitArgs`. Set, it is applied (local config at init/clone, env at
  commit). Unset, go-gitutil passes nothing and git resolves it itself (env,
  repo config, global config, then git's own "Please tell me who you are"
  error). go-gitutil does not pre-check for a missing identity: that would
  refuse on every machine whose identity lives in the user-level git config.
- A strict mode that refuses to fall back to the machine's config is an
  opt-in boolean on the args, never the default.
- go-gitutil bakes in no fixture defaults. The constants are go-fsfix's
  (Q5 → go-fsfix), exported and overridable per fixture:

  | Value | Default |
  |---|---|
  | Author/committer name | `FSFix Fixture` |
  | Author/committer email | `fsfix@example.com` (proposed) |
  | Initial commit message | `Initial commit message (fsfix)` |
  | Default branch | `main` |
  | Force add | on |

  Default branch is a real gap today: gomion's test leaves it to the
  machine's `init.defaultBranch`. Force is on in fixtures because the threat
  is the developer's global excludes file (`core.excludesFile`): a global
  ignore of `.endless/` would silently drop fixture files on one machine only.

## Streamer, Repo and how git runs (Q3, Q4)

- One type. `Repo` holds state plus the optional `dt.StdIO` from RepoArgs.
  `Streamer` is deleted along with the package-level `Commit`,
  `StageModuleFiles` and `UnstageAll` wrappers, which only buffered Streamer's
  output. Mike: streaming is for future callers, not nobody; both benefits in
  one type.
- The rule: operations whose output the package parses (status, rev-parse,
  log, diff) always capture, regardless of StdIO. Operations whose output is
  for a human (commit, add, push, clone, checkout) write to StdIO when set and
  otherwise buffer and return it.
- One run function behind GitRunner, Repo and the creation operations,
  taking ctx, dir, env, stdin, `dt.StdIO` and args; raw `exec.Command`
  disappears from OpenRepo and Streamer. (Fact: today there are three paths,
  GitRunner.runGit in run_git.go buffered with stderr wrapped, OpenRepo in repo.go raw with stderr discarded,
  Streamer.Commit in operations.go raw streaming with no ctx.)

## Go-module knowledge leaves go-gitutil

`StageModuleFiles` finds nested `go.mod` files and stages around them. Mike:
"Go module logic should definitely not be in go-gitutil, but instead in
go-goutil." So:

- `FindNestedModules` moves to go-goutil. gomion's `gommod/goutils` becomes
  go-pkgs/go-goutil, package `goutil`; that extraction is a
  gomion task of its own (the package also holds AST diff, API compatibility,
  dependency analysis).
- go-gitutil keeps the git-only pieces: `UnstageAll`, `StageFileContent`
  (hash-object + update-index), and the new `Add` with `Exclude`.
- gomion composes: `goutil.FindNestedModules`, then `repo.UnstageAll`, then
  `repo.Add(AddArgs{Paths: ["."], Exclude: nested})`.

## Naming

- The package renames from `gitutils` to `gitutil`. Mike: standardize on
  singular `util` across go-pkgs, including renaming go-diffutils. go-diffutils
  is not an Endless project; Mike files that where he tracks it.
- Git domain types (branch name, revision, object id) live in go-dt's root
  package with a `Git` prefix (`GitRefName`, `GitRevision`, `GitObjectID`),
  filed as E-2599 in go-dt. go-gitutil's `GitRef` and `RemoteName` move to
  those types in its implementation task.

## Tests (Q6)

- go-gitutil gets a `test/` module per ED-1650; today it has none and its one
  test, diff_parser_test.go, sits beside the code.
- The test module dogfoods go-fsfix repo fixtures. The build-order friction
  (go-gitutil's tests need a go-fsfix built against the new API) is a tooling
  problem, not an architecture one. Existing tasks: gomion E-2561 (command
  managing go.work across directories) and endless E-1192 (go.work generation
  as a standalone tool).

## The "decoy" files, explained

The term came from the E-2546 session, not Mike. gomion's repo_setup_test.go
fixture places `go.mod` files at `dtx/testdata/x/go.mod` and
`.endless/worktrees/a/go.mod`, with module paths literally `ignored/testdata`
and `ignored/endless`. They are negative cases: gomion's layout classifier
must not treat them as modules. They must be committed because gomion reads
tracked files only ("An untracked go.mod is invisible to CI, so it is
invisible here too"). Better name: excluded-path go.mod files.

## Follow-ups filed

- E-2600 (go-gitutil): Reshape Repo with Init, Clone, Add and Commit. Cleans up
  E-2548; blocks E-2568, E-2559 and E-2556; relates to E-2599.
- E-2602 (go-gitutil): Create go-gitutil's test module on go-fsfix fixtures.
  Blocked by E-2600 and E-2568.
- E-2601 (gomion): Extract gommod/goutils into go-goutil.
- Decisions ED-1658 (singular util names), ED-1659 (Repo NewRepo/Open shape,
  one type with optional StdIO), ED-1660 (Go-module knowledge in go-goutil),
  ED-1661 (go-fsfix owns fixture defaults).
- Not filed, for Mike: rename go-diffutils (not an Endless project). Revise
  E-2556's description: go-gitutil already has Commit, UnstageAll and
  InfoStore, StageModuleFiles is removed rather than carried over, so its
  remaining work is deleting gomion's copy, switching imports, and rewriting
  the three StageModuleFiles/UnstageAll/Commit call sites onto Repo methods
  plus goutil.FindNestedModules.

Platitude: separation of concerns, no real alternative; the move is tracked by the go-goutil tasks
Task-level decision (where fixture constants live), not a project decision; recorded in E-2600's analysis and E-2548's outcome
Belongs to gomion, not go-gitutil; refiled there

  offered so callers pick what fits.

# E-2600 plan: reshape go-gitutil's Repo

go-gitutil has no importers and no tags, so every change below is made in
place, with no aliases or deprecated forms. Its first release is v0.1.0.

## Package and dependencies

- Rename the package `gitutils` to `gitutil`. The module path stays
  `github.com/mikeschinkel/go-gitutil`.
- Require go-dt v0.7.2. Bring every `go.mod` to `go 1.27.0` and lint clean
  with golangci-lint v2.15.0.
- Delete go-gitutil's own `GitRef` and `RemoteName`. Use go-dt's git types
  as E-2600's analysis maps them: branch names are `dt.GitBranchName`,
  revisions `dt.GitRevision`, tags `dt.GitTagName`, remotes
  `dt.GitRemoteName`, and `RevParse` returns `dt.GitObjectID`.
- Replace `currentRemote`'s split of `@{upstream}` on '/' with
  `git config branch.<branch>.remote` and `branch.<branch>.merge`.

## One run function

Every git process runs through one unexported function taking the
directory, environment, stdin, a `dt.StdIO` and the git arguments.
`GitRunner.runGit`, `OpenRepo`'s raw `exec.Command` and `Streamer` all go
through it or go away. Commands whose output go-gitutil parses always
capture it. Commands that print for a person stream to `StdIO` when it is
set.

`Repo.Run(ctx, gitArgs ...string) (string, error)` exports that function
for git commands go-gitutil has no method for, with the Repo's settings.

## RepoArgs

`RepoArgs` holds the settings that last for a Repo's whole life:

- `StdIO dt.StdIO`. Nil means output is captured and not shown.
- `Env []string` of `KEY=VALUE`, applied after the base environment.
- `GitPath dt.Filepath`. Empty means `git` is found on `PATH`.
- `Strict bool`. Isolated mode (below).

`NewRepo(dir dt.DirPath, args *RepoArgs) *Repo` builds a Repo without
running git. `(*Repo).Open(ctx, *OpenArgs)` replaces `OpenRepo`, which is
removed.

### Per-call RepoArgs (P1)

Every operation that exists both as a Repo method and as a package-level
function has one Args type, which embeds `RepoArgs` and is the last
parameter. When a method gets a non-zero embedded `RepoArgs`, it combines
it with the Repo's settings for that one call:

- `StdIO`: the call's value replaces the Repo's when it is non-nil.
- `Env`: the call's entries come after the Repo's, so a repeated key takes
  the call's value.
- `GitPath`: the call's value replaces the Repo's when it is non-empty.
- `Strict`: true turns isolated mode on for the call. A call cannot turn a
  strict Repo's isolation off.

`Open`, `Init` and `Clone` as package-level functions build their Repo
from the embedded `RepoArgs`, so the returned Repo keeps those settings.
Every other package-level function is `NewRepo(dir, nil)` followed by the
method.

### Isolated mode (Strict)

With `Strict`, every git process gets an environment built from nothing,
with none of the parent process's variables:

- `HOME` set to an empty directory that go-gitutil creates and removes;
- `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`;
- `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`, so only local remotes work;
- `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`;
- then `RepoArgs.Env`.

Each process also gets `-c user.useConfigOnly=true`, so git never guesses
an identity from the user name and host name. Strict requires `GitPath`
and fails before running git when it is empty. `PATH` is not passed: git
run by full path needs none.

## Creating repos

- `(*Repo).Init(ctx, *InitArgs)` and `gitutil.Init(ctx, dir, *InitArgs)
  (*Repo, error)`. `InitArgs{RepoArgs; Branch dt.GitBranchName; Identity
  *dt.Mailbox; Config map[string]string}`. go-gitutil applies `Config`
  right after `git init` through the code `SetConfig` uses.
- `(*Repo).Clone(ctx, src, *CloneArgs)` and `gitutil.Clone(ctx, src, dir,
  *CloneArgs) (*Repo, error)`. `CloneArgs{RepoArgs; Local, NoCheckout,
  Bare bool; Branch dt.GitBranchName; Identity *dt.Mailbox; Config
  map[string]string}`. `Config` is passed as `git clone -c key=value`, so
  it applies during the clone's fetch and is written into the new repo.
- `Identity` writes `user.name` and `user.email` into the repo's local
  config. Config keys are applied in sorted order.
- `cached_worktree.go`'s `cloneLocalRepo` uses `Clone`.

## Config

`(*Repo).SetConfig(ctx, key, value string) error` and
`(*Repo).GetConfig(ctx, key string) (string, error)` read and write the
repo's local config.

## Add and Commit

- `(*Repo).Add(ctx, *AddArgs)`. `AddArgs{Paths []dt.RelFilepath; Exclude
  []dt.RelDirPath; All, Force bool}`. Each `Exclude` entry becomes a
  `:(exclude)<dir>/` pathspec.
- `(*Repo).Commit(ctx, *CommitArgs)`. `CommitArgs{Message string; Author,
  Committer *dt.Mailbox; AuthorDate, CommitterDate *time.Time;
  AllowEmpty bool}`, passed as `GIT_AUTHOR_*` and `GIT_COMMITTER_*`
  environment variables:
  - nil `Author`: nothing is passed, so git resolves it;
  - nil `Committer`: uses `Author`;
  - nil `AuthorDate`: git uses the current time;
  - nil `CommitterDate`: uses `AuthorDate`.
- go-gitutil refuses an identity (`Identity`, `Author`, `Committer`) whose
  `DisplayName` is empty, before running git.
- `Streamer`, the package-level `Commit`, `StageModuleFiles` and
  `UnstageAll` are deleted. `UnstageAll` and `StageFileContent` stay as
  Repo methods. `FindNestedModules` stays until E-2608 moves it.

## Methods without Open (W2)

Methods that need only the directory run on a Repo that has not been
opened. Methods that read the current branch or its upstream (the Repo's
`Branch` or `Remote`) return an error on an unopened Repo. Each method's
doc comment says whether it needs `Open`.

The package-level `Status`, `StageFiles`, `StageFileContent`,
`IgnoredFiles`, `LsFilesRaw`, `UnstageFiles`, `ExportStagedFiles`,
`FindRepoRoot` and `InfoDir` become Repo methods, and each package-level
form becomes a wrapper over its method. Each takes one Args type that
embeds `RepoArgs`, last. `AppendToGitignore` and `AppendToGitExclude`
run no git and stay as they are.

## Worktrees

`AddWorktreeArgs{Path dt.DirPath; Branch dt.GitBranchName; Base
dt.GitRevision; Force, ReuseBranch bool}`. With `ReuseBranch` set and the
branch existing, `AddWorktree` checks it out. Otherwise it creates the
branch with `-b`, as today.

## Read side

- `(*Repo).CommitCount(ctx, dt.GitRevision) (int, error)`.
- `(*Repo).TreeEntry(ctx, dt.GitRevision, dt.RelFilepath) (TreeEntry,
  error)`. `TreeEntry` holds the mode, object type, `dt.GitObjectID` and
  path. A gitlink has mode `160000`.

## Tests

The `test/` module covers each item above against real git repos created
in temporary directories, including a strict-mode test that sets a hostile
environment (`HOME` with a `.gitconfig`, `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`) and
shows none of it reaches git.

# E-2600 plan: reshape go-gitutil's Repo

go-gitutil has no importers and no tags, so every change below is made in
place, with no aliases or deprecated forms. Its first release is v0.1.0.

## Package and dependencies

- Rename the package `gitutils` to `gitutil`. The module path stays
  `github.com/mikeschinkel/go-gitutil`.
- Require go-dt v0.7.2. Bring every `go.mod` to `go 1.27.0` and lint clean
  with golangci-lint v2.15.0.
- Delete go-gitutil's own `GitRef` and `RemoteName`. Use go-dt's git types
  as E-2600's analysis maps them: branch names are `dt.GitBranchName`,
  revisions `dt.GitRevision`, tags `dt.GitTagName`, remotes
  `dt.GitRemoteName`, and `RevParse` returns `dt.GitObjectID`.
- Replace `currentRemote`'s split of `@{upstream}` on '/' with
  `git config branch.<branch>.remote` and `branch.<branch>.merge`.

## One run function

Every git process runs through one unexported function taking the
directory, environment, stdin, a `dt.StdIO` and the git arguments.
`GitRunner.runGit`, `OpenRepo`'s raw `exec.Command` and `Streamer` all go
through it or go away. Commands whose output go-gitutil parses always
capture it. Commands that print for a person stream to `StdIO` when it is
set.

`Repo.Run(ctx, gitArgs ...string) (string, error)` exports that function
for git commands go-gitutil has no method for, with the Repo's settings.

## RepoArgs

`RepoArgs` holds the settings that last for a Repo's whole life:

- `StdIO dt.StdIO`. Nil means output is captured and not shown.
- `Env []string` of `KEY=VALUE`, applied after the base environment.
- `GitPath dt.Filepath`. Empty means `git` is found on `PATH`.
- `Strict bool`. Isolated mode (below).

`NewRepo(dir dt.DirPath, args *RepoArgs) *Repo` builds a Repo without
running git. `(*Repo).Open(ctx, *OpenArgs)` replaces `OpenRepo`, which is
removed.

### Per-call RepoArgs (P1)

Every operation that exists both as a Repo method and as a package-level
function has one Args type, which embeds `RepoArgs` and is the last
parameter. When a method gets a non-zero embedded `RepoArgs`, it combines
it with the Repo's settings for that one call:

- `StdIO`: the call's value replaces the Repo's when it is non-nil.
- `Env`: the call's entries come after the Repo's, so a repeated key takes
  the call's value.
- `GitPath`: the call's value replaces the Repo's when it is non-empty.
- `Strict`: true turns isolated mode on for the call. A call cannot turn a
  strict Repo's isolation off.

`Open`, `Init` and `Clone` as package-level functions build their Repo
from the embedded `RepoArgs`, so the returned Repo keeps those settings.
Every other package-level function is `NewRepo(dir, nil)` followed by the
method.

### Isolated mode (Strict)

With `Strict`, every git process gets an environment built from nothing,
with none of the parent process's variables:

- `HOME` set to an empty directory that go-gitutil creates and removes;
- `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`;
- `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`, so only local remotes work;
- `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`;
- then `RepoArgs.Env`.

Each process also gets `-c user.useConfigOnly=true`, so git never guesses
an identity from the user name and host name. Strict requires `GitPath`
and fails before running git when it is empty. `PATH` is not passed: git
run by full path needs none.

## Creating repos

- `(*Repo).Init(ctx, *InitArgs)` and `gitutil.Init(ctx, dir, *InitArgs)
  (*Repo, error)`. `InitArgs{RepoArgs; Branch dt.GitBranchName; Identity
  *dt.Mailbox; Config map[string]string}`. go-gitutil applies `Config`
  right after `git init` through the code `SetConfig` uses.
- `(*Repo).Clone(ctx, src, *CloneArgs)` and `gitutil.Clone(ctx, src, dir,
  *CloneArgs) (*Repo, error)`. `CloneArgs{RepoArgs; Local, NoCheckout,
  Bare bool; Branch dt.GitBranchName; Identity *dt.Mailbox; Config
  map[string]string}`. `Config` is passed as `git clone -c key=value`, so
  it applies during the clone's fetch and is written into the new repo.
- `Identity` writes `user.name` and `user.email` into the repo's local
  config. Config keys are applied in sorted order.
- `cached_worktree.go`'s `cloneLocalRepo` uses `Clone`.

## Config

`(*Repo).SetConfig(ctx, key, value string) error` and
`(*Repo).GetConfig(ctx, key string) (string, error)` read and write the
repo's local config.

## Add and Commit

- `(*Repo).Add(ctx, *AddArgs)`. `AddArgs{Paths []dt.RelFilepath; Exclude
  []dt.RelDirPath; All, Force bool}`. Each `Exclude` entry becomes a
  `:(exclude)<dir>/` pathspec.
- `(*Repo).Commit(ctx, *CommitArgs)`. `CommitArgs{Message string; Author,
  Committer *dt.Mailbox; AuthorDate, CommitterDate *time.Time;
  AllowEmpty bool}`, passed as `GIT_AUTHOR_*` and `GIT_COMMITTER_*`
  environment variables:
  - nil `Author`: nothing is passed, so git resolves it;
  - nil `Committer`: uses `Author`;
  - nil `AuthorDate`: git uses the current time;
  - nil `CommitterDate`: uses `AuthorDate`.
- go-gitutil refuses an identity (`Identity`, `Author`, `Committer`) whose
  `DisplayName` is empty, before running git.
- `Streamer`, the package-level `Commit`, `StageModuleFiles` and
  `UnstageAll` are deleted. `UnstageAll` and `StageFileContent` stay as
  Repo methods. `FindNestedModules` stays until E-2608 moves it.

## Methods without Open (W2)

Methods that need only the directory run on a Repo that has not been
opened. Methods that read the current branch or its upstream (the Repo's
`Branch` or `Remote`) return an error on an unopened Repo. Each method's
doc comment says whether it needs `Open`.

The package-level `Status`, `StageFiles`, `StageFileContent`,
`IgnoredFiles`, `LsFilesRaw`, `UnstageFiles`, `ExportStagedFiles`,
`FindRepoRoot` and `InfoDir` become Repo methods, and each package-level
form becomes a wrapper over its method. Each takes one Args type that
embeds `RepoArgs`, last. `AppendToGitignore` and `AppendToGitExclude`
run no git and stay as they are.

## Worktrees

`AddWorktreeArgs{Path dt.DirPath; Branch dt.GitBranchName; Base
dt.GitRevision; Force, ReuseBranch bool}`. With `ReuseBranch` set and the
branch existing, `AddWorktree` checks it out. Otherwise it creates the
branch with `-b`, as today.

## Read side

- `(*Repo).CommitCount(ctx, dt.GitRevision) (int, error)`.
- `(*Repo).TreeEntry(ctx, dt.GitRevision, dt.RelFilepath) (TreeEntry,
  error)`. `TreeEntry` holds the mode, object type, `dt.GitObjectID` and
  path. A gitlink has mode `160000`.

## Tests

The `test/` module covers each item above against real git repos created
in temporary directories, including a strict-mode test that sets a hostile
environment (`HOME` with a `.gitconfig`, `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`) and
shows none of it reaches git.

  `git config branch.<branch>.remote` and `branch.<branch>.merge`.

## One run function

Every git process runs through one unexported function taking the
directory, environment, stdin, a `dt.StdIO` and the git arguments.
`GitRunner.runGit`, `OpenRepo`'s raw `exec.Command` and `Streamer` all go
through it or go away. Commands whose output go-gitutil parses always
capture it. Commands that print for a person stream to `StdIO` when it is
set.

`Repo.Run(ctx, gitArgs ...string) (string, error)` exports that function
for git commands go-gitutil has no method for, with the Repo's settings.

## RepoArgs

`RepoArgs` holds the settings that last for a Repo's whole life:

- `StdIO dt.StdIO`. Nil means output is captured and not shown.
- `Env []string` of `KEY=VALUE`, applied after the base environment.
- `GitPath dt.Filepath`. Empty means `git` is found on `PATH`.
- `Strict bool`. Isolated mode (below).

`NewRepo(dir dt.DirPath, args *RepoArgs) *Repo` builds a Repo without
running git. `(*Repo).Open(ctx, *OpenArgs)` replaces `OpenRepo`, which is
removed.

### Per-call RepoArgs (P1)

Every operation that exists both as a Repo method and as a package-level
function has one Args type, which embeds `RepoArgs` and is the last
parameter. When a method gets a non-zero embedded `RepoArgs`, it combines
it with the Repo's settings for that one call:

- `StdIO`: the call's value replaces the Repo's when it is non-nil.
- `Env`: the call's entries come after the Repo's, so a repeated key takes
  the call's value.
- `GitPath`: the call's value replaces the Repo's when it is non-empty.
- `Strict`: true turns isolated mode on for the call. A call cannot turn a
  strict Repo's isolation off.

`Open`, `Init` and `Clone` as package-level functions build their Repo
from the embedded `RepoArgs`, so the returned Repo keeps those settings.
Every other package-level function is `NewRepo(dir, nil)` followed by the
method.

### Isolated mode (Strict)

With `Strict`, every git process gets an environment built from nothing,
with none of the parent process's variables:

- `HOME` set to the path of an empty directory that go-gitutil creates and
  removes. Never an empty or unset `HOME`: tools such as ssh then fall back
  to the home directory in the user database;
- `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`;
- `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`, so only local remotes work;
- `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`;
- then `RepoArgs.Env`.

Each process also gets `-c user.useConfigOnly=true`, so git never guesses
an identity from the user name and host name. Strict requires `GitPath`
and fails before running git when it is empty. `PATH` is not passed: git
run by full path needs none.

## Creating repos

- `(*Repo).Init(ctx, *InitArgs)` and `gitutil.Init(ctx, dir, *InitArgs)
  (*Repo, error)`. `InitArgs{RepoArgs; Branch dt.GitBranchName; Identity
  *dt.Mailbox; Config map[string]string}`. go-gitutil applies `Config`
  right after `git init` through the code `SetConfig` uses.
- `(*Repo).Clone(ctx, src, *CloneArgs)` and `gitutil.Clone(ctx, src, dir,
  *CloneArgs) (*Repo, error)`. `CloneArgs{RepoArgs; Local, NoCheckout,
  Bare bool; Branch dt.GitBranchName; Identity *dt.Mailbox; Config
  map[string]string}`. `Config` is passed as `git clone -c key=value`, so
  it applies during the clone's fetch and is written into the new repo.
- `Identity` writes `user.name` and `user.email` into the repo's local
  config. Config keys are applied in sorted order.
- `cached_worktree.go`'s `cloneLocalRepo` uses `Clone`.

## Config

`(*Repo).SetConfig(ctx, key, value string) error` and
`(*Repo).GetConfig(ctx, key string) (string, error)` read and write the
repo's local config.

## Add and Commit

- `(*Repo).Add(ctx, *AddArgs)`. `AddArgs{Paths []dt.RelFilepath; Exclude
  []dt.RelDirPath; All, Force bool}`. Each `Exclude` entry becomes a
  `:(exclude)<dir>/` pathspec.
- `(*Repo).Commit(ctx, *CommitArgs)`. `CommitArgs{Message string; Author,
  Committer *dt.Mailbox; AuthorDate, CommitterDate *time.Time;
  AllowEmpty bool}`, passed as `GIT_AUTHOR_*` and `GIT_COMMITTER_*`
  environment variables:
  - nil `Author`: nothing is passed, so git resolves it;
  - nil `Committer`: uses `Author`;
  - nil `AuthorDate`: git uses the current time;
  - nil `CommitterDate`: uses `AuthorDate`.
- go-gitutil refuses an identity (`Identity`, `Author`, `Committer`) whose
  `DisplayName` is empty, before running git.
- `Streamer`, the package-level `Commit`, `StageModuleFiles` and
  `UnstageAll` are deleted. `UnstageAll` and `StageFileContent` stay as
  Repo methods. `FindNestedModules` stays until E-2608 moves it.

## Methods without Open (W2)

Methods that need only the directory run on a Repo that has not been
opened. Methods that read the current branch or its upstream (the Repo's
`Branch` or `Remote`) return an error on an unopened Repo. Each method's
doc comment says whether it needs `Open`.

The package-level `Status`, `StageFiles`, `StageFileContent`,
`IgnoredFiles`, `LsFilesRaw`, `UnstageFiles`, `ExportStagedFiles`,
`FindRepoRoot` and `InfoDir` become Repo methods, and each package-level
form becomes a wrapper over its method. Each takes one Args type that
embeds `RepoArgs`, last. `AppendToGitignore` and `AppendToGitExclude`
run no git and stay as they are.

## Worktrees

`AddWorktreeArgs{Path dt.DirPath; Branch dt.GitBranchName; Base
dt.GitRevision; Force, ReuseBranch bool}`. With `ReuseBranch` set and the
branch existing, `AddWorktree` checks it out. Otherwise it creates the
branch with `-b`, as today.

## Read side

- `(*Repo).CommitCount(ctx, dt.GitRevision) (int, error)`.
- `(*Repo).TreeEntry(ctx, dt.GitRevision, dt.RelFilepath) (TreeEntry,
  error)`. `TreeEntry` holds the mode, object type, `dt.GitObjectID` and
  path. A gitlink has mode `160000`.

in temporary directories, including a strict-mode test that sets a hostile
environment (`HOME` with a `.gitconfig`, `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`) and

payload.title: Add commit signal classification
payload.description: Add CommitSignal, a CommitClassifier closure defaulting to Conventional Commits, and SummarizeCommitSignals over commit log entries, so callers get fix, feat and breaking counts
payload.context: Decided by Mike on 2026-11-14 while planning go-goutil's extraction (E-2608, "Q1: C"). gomion's gommod/goutils/commit_signals.go classifies commit messages by the Conventional Commits spec: a `!` before the colon or a `BREAKING CHANGE:`/`BREAKING-CHANGE:` footer is breaking, `feat:` or `feat(scope):` is a feature, `fix:` likewise a fix, and the highest signal across the commits wins (breaking > feat > fix). It took `[]gitutils.CommitLogEntry`, the package's only gitutils import. That parsing knows nothing of Go, and go-gitutil's conventional_commit.go already holds the conventional-commit type table, so the classification belongs here, with the convention pluggable through a closure so a project using another prefix scheme can supply its own. The step that maps a signal to goutil's FindingType (the API-compatibility verdict) stays in gomion, so neither go-goutil nor go-gitutil imports the other.

Shape agreed in the E-2608 planning chat:

	CommitSignalNone     CommitSignal = ""

	CommitSignalBreaking CommitSignal = "breaking"

- conventional_commit.go matched exact prefixes ("feat: "), so `feat(api): x` and `feat!: x` parsed as having no type, while gomion's commit-signal helpers understood scope and `!`. ## Conventional commits
- New `ParseConventionalCommit(subject string) (ConventionalCommit, bool)` in conventional_commit.go: `type(scope)!: description`, type one word of letters, digits or hyphens (the spec allows any noun), scope optional, `!` optional. `ConventionalCommit{Type, Scope string; Breaking bool; Description string}` with `String()` and `PrefixLen()`.
- `ParseConventionalCommitType`, `ComposeConventionalCommitSubject` and `ConventionalCommitPrefixLen` are removed; their callers use the parser, `String` and `PrefixLen`. The type table keeps the names for `ConventionalCommitTypeNames`, which a UI offers as choices; the parser does not require a known type.
- New commit_signal.go: `CommitSignal`, `CommitClassifier`, `ConventionalCommitSignal` (breaking from `!` or a footer line, then feat, then fix, types compared case-insensitively), `CommitSignals` and `SummarizeCommitSignals`. Footer lines start with `BREAKING CHANGE: ` or `BREAKING-CHANGE: `, uppercase only. gomion's gommod/goutils/commit_signals.go is the reference for intent, not for the footer check.

## Ignored paths
- `(*Repo).Ignored(ctx, paths []dt.RelDirPath) ([]dt.RelDirPath, error)`: one `git check-ignore --stdin -z` with each path plus `/` on stdin, NUL-separated; parse the NUL-separated answer back to the given paths. Exit 1 means none ignored. Index-aware (git's default).

- Remove `FindNestedModules` from add_commit.go; go-goutil owns it (E-2608).
- Correct `AddArgs.Force`'s comment.

- In the existing test/ module with its current helpers; E-2602 later moves them to go-fsfix fixtures.

# Plan: first tagged release of go-gitutil

Already true on main, checked rather than redone: root go.mod requires go-diffutils v0.1.0, go-dt v0.7.2 and go-dt/dtx v0.3.0 (each its latest tag) with no replace; every go.mod says go 1.27.0; .gitignore lists go.work and go.work.sum.

## Steps
1. Write README.md: what go-gitutil does, `go get`, a short example of NewRepo, Open and RepoArgs, and what Strict mode isolates. Draw it from doc.go and RepoArgs' doc comment.
2. Remove PLAN-CONDENSED-DIFF-TYPES.md.
3. Run `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories origin/main` to bring in GitHub's LICENSE commit. No force push, no rebase.
4. Generate .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml with `gomion repo setup <repo>`. The installed gomion lacks `repo setup` and gomion's main does not build in its own workspace (teamodal v0.1.0 requires teautils v0.0.0), so build cmd/gomion with a scratch go.work, outside both repos, that adds go-tealeaves/teautils. Don't edit gomion, and don't hand-edit the generated files. Because of E-2627, `--check` exits non-zero on its own arguments, so read its go-gitutil line rather than its exit code.
5. Run GOWORK=off build, vet and test on the root and test/ modules, and golangci-lint v2.15.0 on both.
6. Push main to origin. Create no tag.
7. Watch the first Test run on the pushed commit; it must pass with no warning or notice annotations.
8. Record in the task's notes a proposed version, v0.1.0, and a release description, for the owner to run the Release workflow with.
